title: Set up the project
body:
Set up the app so we can start building.

- A FastAPI app in the `crm` package. `crm.main.create_app(database_path)` returns the app, using a SQLite file at that path. `crm.main:app` is the app for `uvicorn`, using the path in the `CRM_DATABASE` environment variable (default `crm.db`).
- `GET /health` returns `{"status": "ok"}`.
- pytest set up, with `uv run pytest` as the test command.
- GitHub Actions CI that runs the tests on every pull request.
- The README says how to run the app and the tests.

title: Contacts API
body:
We need to store contacts.

- `POST /api/contacts` with `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` and optional `phone` creates a contact and returns it with its `id` (201).
- `GET /api/contacts/{id}` returns one contact. 404 if it does not exist.
- `GET /api/contacts` lists contacts.
- `PATCH /api/contacts/{id}` updates any of the fields.
- `DELETE /api/contacts/{id}` deletes it (204).

Email is required and must look like an email. Two contacts cannot share an email: that is a 409.

title: Paginate and sort the contact list
body: The contact list will get long. Change `GET /api/contacts` to return `{"items": [...], "total": N}` and accept `limit` (default 50, max 200), `offset` and `sort` (`last_name` or `created_at`, newest first for `created_at`).

title: Companies API
body: Contacts work for companies. Add companies with `name` (required) and `domain` (optional, like `acme.com`). Same endpoints as contacts: create (201), get, list (`{items, total}` with `limit` and `offset`), update and delete. Company names must be unique, ignoring case (409).

title: Link contacts to companies
body: A contact can belong to one company. Add `company_id` to contacts (set on create or update; 422 if the company does not exist). `GET /api/companies/{id}/contacts` lists a company's contacts. Deleting a company must not delete its contacts: they just lose the link.

title: Link new contacts to a company by email domain
body: When I add a contact with an email at `acme.com` and we have a company with domain `acme.com`, link them automatically. If I give a `company_id` myself, use that instead.

title: Deals API
body: Track deals. A deal has a `title`, a `value` in whole cents, a `currency` (default `USD`), an optional `company_id` and `contact_id`, and a `stage`: one of `lead`, `qualified`, `proposal`, `won`, `lost` (default `lead`). Create (201), get, list (`{items, total}`), update and delete, under `/api/deals`. The list can be filtered by `stage`.

title: Closed deals
body: When a deal moves to `won` or `lost`, record when it closed as `closed_at`. Closed deals shouldn't be edited by accident.

title: Pipeline summary
body: `GET /api/pipeline` returns, for each stage in order, the number of deals and their total value: `{"stages": [{"stage": "lead", "count": 3, "value": 150000}, ...]}`. Every stage appears, even with zero deals.

title: Activities
body: Log what happens. `POST /api/activities` with a `type` (`note`, `call`, `email` or `meeting`), a `body`, an optional `occurred_at` (default now), and at least one of `contact_id`, `company_id` and `deal_id`. Get, list and delete as for the other records.

title: Contact timeline
body: `GET /api/contacts/{id}/timeline` returns everything that happened with a contact, newest first: their own activities and the activities on their deals.

title: Search
body: `GET /api/search?q=TEXT` finds contacts (by name or email), companies (by name or domain) and deals (by title), ignoring case. It returns `{"contacts": [...], "companies": [...], "deals": [...]}`.

title: Tag contacts
body: Let us tag contacts, for example `vip` or `churn-risk`. `PUT /api/contacts/{id}/tags` with a list of tags replaces a contact's tags, and contacts include their `tags`. `GET /api/contacts?tag=vip` lists only contacts with that tag.

title: Search misses emails with capital letters
body: I think search is case sensitive for emails. Searching for `alice@acme.com` might not find `Alice@Acme.com`.

title: Contacts web pages
body: The team needs a web interface. `GET /contacts` shows a page listing contacts with a search box. `GET /contacts/{id}` shows a contact, their company and their timeline. Plain server-rendered HTML is fine.

title: Deals board
body: `GET /deals` shows a page with one column per stage and the deals in each, with their value.

title: Add contacts from the web
body: Add a form at `GET /contacts/new` that posts to `POST /contacts/new` and creates a contact, then redirects to the new contact's page. Show the errors on the form if the data is invalid.

title: User accounts and API tokens
body:
Everyone has been sharing one login. Add accounts.

- `POST /api/auth/register` with `email` and `password` creates a user (201).
- `POST /api/auth/login` returns `{"token": "..."}`.
- Every other `/api` endpoint, except `/health`, needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Without it: 401.
- Never store passwords in plain text.

title: Deal owners
body: Each deal belongs to the user who created it, as `owner_id`. `GET /api/deals?owner=me` lists only my deals.

title: Sign in to the web pages
body: The web pages should need a sign in too. Add a sign-in form at `/login`. Signed-out visitors to any page get sent there.

title: Import contacts from CSV
body: `POST /api/contacts/import` takes a CSV file upload (field name `file`) with the columns `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` and optional `company`. It returns `{"created": N, "skipped": N, "errors": [{"row": N, "error": "..."}]}`. Skip rows whose email already exists. Create the company if it does not exist yet.

title: Export contacts to CSV
body: `GET /api/contacts/export` downloads all contacts as CSV, with the same columns the import takes, so an export can be imported into a new system.

title: Dashboard numbers
body: `GET /api/reports/summary` returns `contacts`, `companies`, `open_deals` (not won or lost), `open_value`, and `won_value_this_month` (deals won since the first of this month).

title: Deleting a contact loses our history
body: When someone deletes a contact, their activities and deals go with them, and we lose the history. That shouldn't happen.

title: Dashboard page
body: Show the dashboard numbers on the home page, `GET /`, for signed-in users.
